# **0\. How to Read This Guide**

V1.9 keeps the V1.7/V1.8 architecture but repairs the execution gaps. It does not add a disconnected framework. It makes one working system: G-STIC is the master spine; StoryBrand 2 clarifies messaging; the HORO ritual/rhythm story anchors brand meaning; the palette expresses the story; the content and channel system moves the buyer; WhatsApp and PDPs reduce risk; the dashboard decides what scales.

| Part | Purpose |
| :---- | :---- |
| Sections 1-6 | Strategy, G-STIC spine, operating system, and validation priorities |
| Sections 7-13 | Commercial wedge, brand guardrails, product proof, artist collaboration |
| Sections 14-18 | Website, content OS, channels, calendar, media buying, WhatsApp |
| Sections 19-20 | Dashboard, decision board, source validation, case learning, implementation checklists |
| Appendices | Production bible, templates, source notes, final rules |

# **1\. Executive Summary**

HORO V1.9 is the master guide for a controlled 90-day launch of an Egyptian wearable-art brand. HORO should not launch as a broad fashion brand. It should first win one buying situation: meaningful, giftable, artist-made T-shirts for Cairo/Giza adults who want something personal, wearable, and safe to buy online.

***V1.9 thesis: HORO is a rhythm-based passion-wear brand. Every touchpoint should help the buyer express what they feel and buy with confidence.***

| What must be proven | Why it matters | Validation method |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| People understand HORO quickly | Unclear category kills conversion. | 5-buyer test, homepage click map, PDP visits |
| Gift/self-expression intent exists | This is the first commercial wedge. | Gift-route clicks, WhatsApp gift inquiries, first orders |
| Story improves memory | The rhythm story must make HORO easier to remember, not more abstract. | Aided recall, interviews, comment language |
| Price feels justified | Price is a hypothesis. | ATC, objections, conversion, margin |
| Service reduces risk | Egyptian online buying needs reassurance. | WhatsApp close rate, confirmation rate, RTO |
| Post-purchase proof appears | New brands need visible trust. | Reviews, UGC, next-drop interest |

# **2\. Strategic Core**

Marketing is treated as an investment system: create value, communicate value, deliver value, and measure profitable exchange. HORO creates value through product, story, service, community, and operational trust.

| Value type | HORO meaning | Visible proof |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Functional value | Wearable shirt, clear fit, quality print, care, delivery and support. | On-body photos, size guide, print close-up, care note, delivery/exchange clarity |
| Monetary value | The buyer feels the price is justified versus cheap print, custom print, or generic gifts. | Offer ladder, proof ladder, gift-ready packaging, lower first-order risk |
| Psychological value | Identity, emotion, belonging, rhythm, artist meaning, gift recognition. | Design story, ritual/rhythm narrative, artist proof, UGC, recipient framing |

| Competitor type | Buyer comparison | HORO answer |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Cheap printed tee | Lower price and easy substitute. | Original art, curated meaning, proof-first service. |
| Custom print shop | Can print anything. | HORO curates meaning when the buyer has no design. |
| Fashion brand | Better fit/style trust. | HORO adds emotional meaning and gifting context. |
| Gift shop | Packaging and occasion utility. | HORO is useful like clothing and personal like a message. |
| Marketplace seller | Cheap and searchable. | HORO wins through brand, proof, story, and service. |

# **3\. Simple Logic Behind V1.9**

| Plain question | V1.9 answer |
| :---- | :---- |
| What is HORO? | Artist-made passion wear for feelings, identity, rhythm, and meaningful gifts. |
| Why HORO? | The name carries the idea of communal ritual, rhythm, connection, and celebration. |
| Who first? | Cairo/Giza adults with gift or self-expression intent: 25-40 self-expression buyers and 25-45 gift buyers. |
| What comparison must HORO escape? | Being seen as just an expensive printed T-shirt. |
| What creates trust? | Product proof, artist process, size help, payment clarity, delivery clarity, exchange, WhatsApp support, and reviews. |
| What should content do? | Move people through attention, recognition, desire, trust, action, ownership, advocacy, and repeat. |

# **4\. Unified Planning and Validation Spine**

![][image2]

## **4.1 G-STIC as the master system**

| G-STIC step | What it contains | Frameworks folded inside |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Situation | Egypt market reality, customer behavior, competitors, collaborators, context, proof gaps. | 5C, PESTEL, category boundaries, social commerce risk |
| Goals | 90-day proof targets, not vanity targets. | Awareness quality, ATC, conversion, RTO, margin, UGC |
| Strategy | First wedge, target segment, positioning, brand story. | STP, 3Vs, StoryBrand 2 |
| Tactics | Product, price, place, promotion, content, service, creator system. | 4Ps, content jobs, channel playbooks |
| Implementation | Owners, cadence, production, budget, tools, workflows. | Calendar, production bible, WhatsApp scripts |
| Control | Dashboard, stage gates, stop rules, evidence register. | Scale/fix/narrow/pause/pivot |

## **4.2 StoryBrand 2 / Soundbite Strategy inside G-STIC**

V1.9 uses StoryBrand 2 as the messaging lens inside Strategy and Tactics. It does not use the first-edition StoryBrand framework as a separate planning island. The working emphasis is clarity, reduced cognitive load, repeatable soundbites, and a clear next step.

![][image3]

| StoryBrand 2 element | HORO application |
| :---- | :---- |
| Customer as hero | The buyer wants self-expression or a meaningful gift. |
| Problem | Generic gifts, generic tees, and uncertainty about ordering from a young online brand. |
| HORO as guide | HORO shows empathy, taste, proof, and a simple buying path. |
| Plan | Choose a rhythm route, see proof, ask if needed, order confidently. |
| Soundbites | Artist-made passion wear; Wear What You Feel; Find Your Rhythm; We are the canvas. You are the story. |
| CTA | Shop the drop, ask on WhatsApp, choose a gift, join waitlist. |
| Success | The wearer feels seen; the gift feels personal; the order feels safe. |

## **4.3 Design-thinking validation layer**

| Discipline | HORO version | Boundary |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Empathy | 8-12 interviews during first 30 days. | Do not delay launch endlessly. |
| Divergence | 2-3 message/visual options before major assets. | Avoid founder anchoring. |
| Prototype | Rough test before heavy design, shoot, code or spend. | One iteration cycle or explicit override. |
| 5-buyer validation | Show homepage, PDP, and hero creative to target buyers. | Directional, not statistically conclusive. |

# **5\. Operating Spine**

| Operating layer | Purpose | Weekly artifact |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Product proof | Make value visible before price is judged. | Product proof checklist and PDP score |
| Content OS | Turn ideas into buyer-stage assets. | Weekly content board |
| Creative bible | Produce assets consistently and cheaply. | Shot list and asset bank |
| Channel playbooks | Use each platform according to behavior. | Channel calendar and adaptations |
| WhatsApp commerce | Close hesitant buyers without sounding pushy. | Inquiry log and objection library |
| Commercial dashboard | Read performance without vanity bias. | Weekly dashboard |
| Budget control | Prevent overspending before evidence. | Monthly budget gate and CPA review |
| Pilot decision board | Choose scale/fix/narrow/pause/pivot. | Stage-gate decision record |

Operating sequence: prioritize \-\> focus \-\> master \-\> automate \-\> scale. HORO should pick one wedge, focus on few products/routes, master the conversion loop, automate repeatable work, and scale only when proof is visible.

# **7\. First Commercial Wedge**

HORO should first own a narrow buying situation: a buyer wants a gift or self-expression item that feels personal, looks good, and is safer than ordering from an unknown online page.

| Wedge component | Definition | What to avoid |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Meaningful | Expresses a feeling, identity, moment, rhythm, or person. | Decorative designs with no story |
| Giftable | Easy to imagine giving to someone specific. | Packaging or copy that feels careless |
| Artist-made | Original artwork with visible process and credit. | Random downloaded graphic feel |
| Wearable | Works in real outfits and real Cairo contexts. | Art that is too loud or childish |
| Safe to buy | Size, payment, exchange, delivery, WhatsApp, proof. | Beautiful ads with weak service |
| Rhythmic | Fits someone’s daily rhythm and repeated self-expression. | A concept too abstract to enter real life |

# **8\. Brand Definition and Guardrails**

Brand story paragraph: In Balkan and Slavic traditions, Horo is a communal circle dance: a ritual of rhythm, connection, and celebration. HORO translates that symbol into fashion. A shirt becomes a small daily ritual: a way to align what someone feels inside with what they show outside.

| Element | Public rule | Internal rule |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Public line | Wear What You Feel | إلبس اللي بتحس بيه | Use consistently. |
| Brand idea | Find Your Rhythm | Use as campaign and story lens. |
| Supporting line | We are the canvas. You are the story. | Use in About, packaging, launch storytelling. |
| Category shorthand | Passion wear | Use selectively when defining the category. |
| Brand role | Perceptive friend with taste and restraint. | Not meme page, not luxury gatekeeper. |
| Language | Clear English with selective Egyptian Arabic. | Arabic supports service and emotion. |
| Zodiac rule | Entertainment/personality only. | No fortune-telling framing. |
| Artist rule | Artist visible as proof. | Wearer remains the hero. |
| Price rule | Earn price through proof. | Show product, story, service, reviews. |

## **8.2 Photography and visual rules**

| Rule | V1.9 standard |
| :---- | :---- |
| Light | Warm natural light, golden hour, or soft indoor light. |
| Surfaces | Linen, wood, textured walls, paper, Cairo street details, clean home surfaces. |
| People | Real Cairo wearers, unisex styling, varied body representation where possible. |
| Mood | Ritual, rhythm, connection, warmth, grounded self-expression. |

# **9\. Positioning, Segments, and Message**

| Segment | Why it matters | Best route |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 25-40 self-expression buyer | Buys if design feels personal and wearable. | A shirt that says what you feel without explaining. |
| 25-45 gift buyer | Has occasion urgency and can justify a meaningful gift. | A personal gift when normal gifts feel generic. |
| Artist-aware buyer | Values process and originality. | Original artwork you can wear. |
| 18-24 reach/UGC audience | Useful for TikTok, styling, UGC, trend learning. | Which rhythm feels like you today? |
| Selective 40+ tasteful buyer | Future potential after trust matures. | A meaningful gift, presented properly. |

| Order | Message | Reason |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Artist-made T-shirts for feelings, identity, rhythm, and meaningful gifts. | Explains category. |
| 2 | Personal without being generic. | Explains emotional/gift value. |
| 3 | Looks wearable in real life. | Prevents “nice idea, not wearable” objection. |
| 4 | Visible proof: fabric, print, size, delivery, exchange. | Reduces first-order risk. |
| 5 | Find Your Rhythm. | Makes story memorable. |

# **10\. Buyer Journey and Trust Assets**

| Stage | Trust asset | Build order |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Attention | Clear product image \+ one-line category explanation. | Before paid traffic |
| Recognition | Mood/gift/rhythm hooks and route labels. | Before homepage scale |
| Desire | On-body styling, fit proof, close-ups. | Before product ads |
| Trust | Artist/process, fabric, print, size, payment, delivery, exchange, reviews. | Before scaling spend |
| Action | Simple PDP, WhatsApp support, cart clarity. | Before launch |
| Ownership | Packaging, care card, delivery updates, support. | During first orders |
| Advocacy | Review request, UGC permission, next-drop invitation. | After delivery |

***Do not ask ads to solve trust gaps. Build product pages, size guidance, service clarity, artist proof, and first reviews before increasing spend.***

# **11\. Product and Offer Ladder**

| Offer level | Role | Recommendation | Risk |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Entry tee | First-order proof | Use only if margin allows. | Can train discount behavior. |
| Core artist tee | Main line | Main price once product and artist proof are visible. | Weak proof makes price feel high. |
| Gift-ready tee | Higher perceived value | Add note/packaging only if cost controlled. | Packaging can erode margin. |
| Limited drop | Premium test | Use after UGC and delivery confidence. | Premium before proof may fail. |
| Bundle | AOV support | Use for self \+ gift or pair gifting. | Heavy discounting weakens value. |

# **12\. Product Readiness and Quality System**

| Readiness item | Minimum standard | Proof asset |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Blank T-shirt | Consistent fit, fabric weight, stitching, shrinkage behavior. | Fabric close-up, size chart, care note |
| Print | Consistent quality, correct placement, no peeling on test sample. | Print close-up, stretch/wash demo |
| Size system | Clear measurements, model references, fit notes. | Size guide, WhatsApp script |
| Packaging | Clean, gift-safe, cost-controlled. | Packaging photo, unboxing clip |
| Delivery | Clear Cairo/Giza ETA and confirmation process. | Delivery policy block |
| Exchange | Plain, operationally realistic. | Exchange policy block |
| PDP proof | Every product has real media before heavy promotion. | Photo/video checklist |

# **13\. Artist Collaboration and Art-Direction System**

| Step | Question | Output |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Brief | What feeling, rhythm, person, or gift moment does the design serve? | One-page artist brief |
| Concept | Can a buyer recognize themselves or someone they know? | 2-3 rough directions |
| Wearability | Would this work on a shirt in real life? | Mockup \+ styling test |
| Cultural check | Any religious, political, gender, class, or zodiac sensitivity? | Approval/revision note |
| Production check | Will the print reproduce well? | Print sample approval |
| Story capture | Can we explain the design in one short caption? | Design story bullets |
| Rights | Do we have usage rights and attribution terms? | Agreement \+ asset folder |

# **15\. Content Operating System by Buying Stage**

Each post must have one job, one segment, one message, one proof asset, one CTA, one KPI, and one reuse path.

| Pillar | Purpose | Example | Primary KPI |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Meaning / Identity | Create recognition. | For the person who feels too much but says little. | Saves, shares |
| Gift Moments | Create usefulness and occasion urgency. | A gift for the friend who is impossible to buy for. | Gift clicks, WhatsApp |
| Artist & Process Proof | Differentiate from cheap print. | Sketch to artwork to shirt. | Saves, product clicks |
| Product Proof | Reduce quality/price risk. | Fabric, print, size, wash, packaging. | ATC, FAQ clicks |
| Styling / Wearability | Make it feel usable. | 3 ways to style one HORO tee. | Watch time, clicks |
| Why HORO, not X? | Handle comparison without attacking. | Custom print vs artist-made tee. | Comments, PDP clicks |
| Community / UGC | Build trust after buyers. | Customer photo, review, unboxing. | UGC, conversion |
| Drop / Offer | Create action. | First artist drop is open \- payment options shown at checkout. | Orders, CPA |

| Content type | Job | HORO examples |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Growth | Make people follow, save, share, remember. | Meaning hooks, design interpretation, artist BTS, styling, polls, trends |
| Conversion | Make people click, ask, ATC, buy. | Product proof, gift guides, comparison, drop posts, WhatsApp CTA |
| Confirmation | Help interested buyers feel safer. | Reviews, size guide, delivery proof, payment clarity |
| Loyalty | Bring buyers back or create advocacy. | Care tips, review request, next-drop invite, win-back |

| Sales structure | Sequence |
| :---- | :---- |
| Direct sales | Need as a question \-\> HORO advantage \-\> proof \-\> one CTA. |
| Offer-driven | Opportunity \-\> value \-\> proof \-\> detail \-\> urgency \-\> CTA. |
| Storytelling | Emotional situation \-\> design meaning \-\> proof and wearability \-\> next step. |

## **17.4 Corrected budget recommendation**

| Budget level | Recommended range | Use | Decision rule |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Serious lean monthly start | EGP 20k-35k/month | Freelancer \+ AI \+ basic shoot \+ small creative testing. | Use for first 4-6 weeks. |
| 90-day serious lean pilot | EGP 75k-125k | Enough for proof assets, content, testing, WhatsApp, dashboard. | Default V1.9 plan. |
| Month 3 moderate proof | EGP 40k-65k/month | Step up only after real order proof. | Use if CPA/order quality/margin are acceptable. |
| Stronger scale push | EGP 65k-90k+/month | Only when product-message-channel fit is visible. | Scale by 20-30% every 2-3 days, not suddenly. |

## **17.5 Media gate stop/fix rules**

| Phase | Budget range | Use | Stop/fix rule |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Before paid selling | 0-2k testing | Warm pixels, verify events. | Do not move on if PDP/tracking/checkout unclear. |
| Creative testing | 300-500 EGP/day for 7 days | Test hooks and content angles. | Pause if clicks or understanding are weak. |
| Conversion pilot | 500-1,500 EGP/day for 10-14 days | Sales \+ WhatsApp \+ retargeting. | Fix if CPA exceeds contribution or order quality is poor. |
| Scale | \+20-30% every 2-3 days only on proof | Scale winners carefully. | Stop if RTO rises, margin breaks, or fatigue appears. |

# **18\. WhatsApp Commerce Operating Model**

| Situation | Approved response logic |
| :---- | :---- |
| Size question | Ask height/weight/preferred fit if needed; send size chart; recommend one size clearly; mention exchange briefly. |
| Gift help | Ask occasion, recipient style/age, size confidence, delivery date; recommend 2-3 products maximum. |
| Price objection | Acknowledge; explain original art, fabric/print proof, packaging/service; avoid arguing. |
| Payment question | Confirm available methods and order confirmation; avoid unconditional COD claims. |
| Exchange question | Explain simple exchange conditions plainly. |
| Delivery delay | Apologize, provide updated ETA, offer choice if delay is significant. |
| Review request | After delivery and satisfaction; ask permission to repost photo/review. |

| Metric | Formula | Use |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Response time | Median time to first reply. | Service quality |
| Inquiry-to-order | Orders from WhatsApp / qualified inquiries. | Closing quality |
| Gift inquiry share | Gift inquiries / total inquiries. | Wedge validation |
| Size anxiety | Size questions / qualified inquiries. | Sizing/PDP improvement |
| Confirmation rate | Confirmed orders / manual-confirmation orders. | Order quality |
| RTO/cancellation | Failed or cancelled orders / total orders. | Risk control |

# **19\. Unit Economics, KPI Dashboard, and Pilot Decision Board**

| Dashboard block | Metrics | Decision |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Traffic quality | Sessions, source, landing page, engagement. | Which channel deserves more attention. |
| Product interest | PDP views, product clicks, saves. | Which products/messages deserve testing. |
| Cart behavior | ATC, checkout start, abandoned cart. | PDP or checkout fixes. |
| Sales | Orders, conversion, CPA, AOV. | Spend control. |
| Order quality | Confirmation, cancellation, RTO, delivery issues. | Operational risk. |
| Trust proof | Reviews, UGC, photo permissions, waitlist. | Brand proof readiness. |
| Content quality | Hook retention, watch time, saves, shares, product clicks. | Creative iteration. |
| Margin | Gross margin, contribution, discount share. | Scale or stop. |

| Decision | Trigger | Action |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Scale | Green across conversion, order quality, margin, proof loop. | Increase spend and inventory gradually. |
| Fix | Interest exists but trust or UX fails. | Repair PDP, proof, WhatsApp, offer, sizing. |
| Narrow | One segment/theme wins clearly. | Focus product/content/spend there. |
| Pause | High RTO/cancellations or margin damage. | Stop spend until cause is fixed. |
| Pivot | Engagement but no buying after fixes. | Change product, price, route, or target. |

# **20\. Evidence, Case Learning, and Implementation Checklists**

## **20.1 Source-to-claim validation table**

| Claim area | Source basis | Confidence / limit |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| StoryBrand 2 / Soundbite Strategy | Current StoryBrand site foregrounds clarity, customer engagement, repeatable soundbites, and lowering cognitive load. | Medium-high; use as messaging lens, not a full proof of market demand. |
| G-STIC / social strategy | Strategic social media management sources emphasize audience research, objectives, key messages, tactics, scheduling, monitoring, and measurement. | High as process guidance. |
| Digital marketing sequence | Digital marketing source stresses segmentation and channel selection before content and measuring behavioral change. | High as planning discipline. |
| Purchasing psychology | Purchasing-decision source warns that effects depend on context and encourages experiments. | High as caution against overclaiming. |
| UX/process | UX/Figma source supports user-centered process, prototyping, journey/flow documentation, accessibility, and iteration. | High as implementation principle. |
| Egypt category and personas | HORO market definition and Cairo Go/No-Go documents define self-expression apparel, gifting, COD/trust, and local competitors. | Medium-high; still requires pilot validation. |
| Content and budget | Previous HORO content and budget plans provide cadence, channel roles, and EGP ranges. | Medium; V1.9 updates the budget upward for visual proof needs. |
| Color psychology | Brand associations are designed from story and should be tested with buyers. | Medium; not universal law. |

## **20.2 Same-industry case-learning cards**

![][image7]

| Case pattern | Observed lesson | HORO application |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Local statement tees | Identity and local cultural references can create attention. | Use rhythm/identity language, but keep product proof strong. |
| Custom print shops | They win price and convenience. | HORO must explain curation, artist proof, and gift service. |
| Personalized gift brands | Packaging, occasion and recipient framing increase perceived value. | Build gift hub, packaging proof, and WhatsApp gift help. |
| Streetwear drop brands | Drops focus attention and reduce choice overload. | Use limited drops only when trust and stock discipline exist. |
| Creator-led fashion | Real people reduce online buying risk. | Use micro-creators for fit, styling and proof, not only reach. |
| Artist-led merch | Process makes originality visible. | Show artist process but keep wearer as hero. |

| Movement clips | 5 x 3-5 seconds | Reels/TikTok edits |
| Print close-up | 2 | Trust post, PDP proof |

| UGC request card | 1 | Post-purchase proof loop |

| Second | What happens |
| :---- | :---- |
| 0-2 | Hook: buyer pain, identity line, gift situation, or visual surprise. |
| 2-6 | Show product clearly on body or in hand. |
| 6-12 | Add meaning/proof: artist, print close-up, styling, gift use. |
| 12-18 | Reassure: payment clarity, size help, exchange, delivery, packaging. |
| 18-25 | CTA: shop, ask on WhatsApp, vote, save, join waitlist. |

# **Appendix B. Channel Execution Templates**

| Template | Structure |
| :---- | :---- |
| Instagram Reel | Hook text on-screen \+ product within 2 seconds \+ proof/detail \+ CTA in caption/product tag. |
| Instagram Carousel | Slide 1 hook, slide 2 product, slide 3 meaning, slide 4 proof, slide 5 gift/size, slide 6 CTA. |
| TikTok POV | POV hook \+ relatable situation \+ product reveal \+ short proof \+ comment question. |
| Facebook trust post | Practical headline \+ 2-3 reassurance bullets \+ product photo \+ WhatsApp CTA. |
| WhatsApp Status | Product image \+ short offer/proof \+ “Reply for size help”. |
| Forum/group question | Neutral research question \+ no sales link \+ ask for honest preference. |

# **Appendix E. Buyer Interview Questions**

* What do you think HORO sells after seeing this page or post for 5 seconds?  
* Would you buy it for yourself, as a gift, both, or neither?  
* What would you compare the price against?  
* What proof would you need before ordering?  
* Does the ritual/rhythm story make the brand more meaningful or too abstract?  
* Which color combination feels most like HORO: Root/Breath/Pulse or something else?  
* Which design would you save, share, or ask about?  
* What would stop you from ordering today?  
* What would make it gift-worthy?

| Source | How V1.9 used it | Limit |

| StoryBrand official site / StoryBrand 2 Soundbite Strategy | Used for clarity, low cognitive load, repeatable soundbites, and direct CTA logic. | Not a substitute for buyer testing. |
| Strategic Social Media Management | Used for audience research, goals, key messages, tactics, measurement, scheduling, content creation, risk and customer service. | General framework; adapt to Egypt. |
| Digital Marketing: Tools, Techniques and Best Practices | Used for segmentation-first planning, channel selection, content distribution, and measurement of behavior. | General digital marketing logic. |
| 33 Phenomena of Purchasing Decisions | Used for choice overload, reference price, social norms, scarcity caution, and experiment-first thinking. | Effects are context-dependent. |
| UX Design with Figma | Used for prototyping, user journeys, user flows, accessibility and iteration. | Implementation still needs testing on actual website. |
| HORO market definition \+ Cairo Go/No-Go | Used for category boundaries, gift/self-expression demand, local alternatives and trust/COD context. | Secondary research; pilot data required. |
| HORO 90-Day Content Plan | Used for channel roles, content pillars, cadence and one-post job logic. | Updated by V1.9 visual/story system. |
| HORO Budget Plan \+ latest review | Used for proof-gated spend, freelancer \+ AI model, and media buying gates. | V1.9 corrects lean budget upward for reliable visuals. |
| Fashion communication and digital marketing sources | Used for fashion storytelling, digital fashion communication, eWOM/reviews, customer journey and social-commerce context. | Needs ongoing platform updates. |

# **Final Operating Rules**

| Rule set A | Rule set B |
| :---- | :---- |
| Do not compete as broad fashion before winning one clear buying situation. | Do not scale engagement without clicks, inquiries, orders, proof, or margin. |
| Do not ask paid ads to solve product, trust, service, or PDP weaknesses. | Do not buy heavy inventory before product-message-channel fit appears. |
| Do not hide behind emotional language when buyers ask practical questions. | Do not make HORO look like a custom print shop unless the offer is intentionally custom printing. |
| Do not use first-edition StoryBrand as the main label; V1.9 uses StoryBrand 2 / Soundbite Strategy language. | Do not use “Feel You What Wear.” The public line is “Wear What You Feel | إلبس اللي بتحس بيه.” |
| Do not use AI-generated visuals or copy without human review for taste, truth, cultural fit, and brand consistency. | Run weekly scale/fix decisions and protect story, proof, service, and rhythm coherence. |
